name: Opportunity Rover
goal: Search for geological evidence of ancient liquid water and assess past Martian habitability.
story: Landed on Mars in 2004 for a planned 90-day mission, Opportunity explored the Red Planet for nearly 15 years, traveling 28 miles. It discovered hematite blueberries and gypsum veins—conclusive proof that liquid water once flowed across Mars surface. A planet-wide dust storm in 2018 cut off its solar power, leaving the silent geologist on Meridiani Planum.

evidence.text: Opportunity discovered hematite blueberries and gypsum veins, proving liquid water was long-standing on ancient Mars.
evidence.label: confirmed
